1.note: The author assumes that readers will know that by **the king of Samaria**, he is not referring to a king who ruled the city of Samaria, but to Ahab, the king who ruled Israel from Samaria as his capital city. You could say that explicitly if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [the king who ruled Israel from the city of Samaria]

2.note: Ahab is using **in your eyes** as a common expression of the culture to mean “in your judgment” or “in your opinion.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [in your judgment]

2.q: תְּנָ⁠ה־לִּ֨⁠י אֶֽת־כַּרְמְ⁠ךָ֜ וִֽ⁠יהִי־לִ֣⁠י לְ⁠גַן־יָרָ֗ק כִּ֣י ה֤וּא קָרוֹב֙ אֵ֣צֶל בֵּיתִ֔⁠י
2.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you could reverse the order of these phrases, since the second phrase gives the reason for the result that the first phrase describes. Alternate translation: [Since your vineyard is near beside my house, give it to me, and it will be to me for a garden of vegetables]

3.note: Naboth is using a common expression of this culture to express his horror at the idea that Ahab has just described. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. If you have already translated the book of 1 Samuel, see how you translated the similar expression in 1 Samuel 24:6. Alternate translation: [Far be it from me to sin against Yahweh by giving]
To translate this expression here and in the next verse, see how you translated the similar expression in 1:21. Alternate translation: [my ancestors]

4.note: Here, **the word** represents what Naboth said by using words. If it would be clearer in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [what Naboth the Jezreelite had said to him]

The author is using one kind of food, **bread**, to mean food in general. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly, here and in verses 5 and 7. Alternate translation: [food]

5.note: Jezebel is using **What is this** as a common expression of her culture to ask Ahab to explain his conduct. If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [What’s going on here?]

6.note: Ahab is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [I am sullen and not eating bread because]

6.q: וָ⁠אֹ֣מַר ל֗⁠וֹ תְּנָ⁠ה־לִּ֤⁠י אֶֽת־כַּרְמְ⁠ךָ֙ בְּ⁠כֶ֔סֶף א֚וֹ אִם־חָפֵ֣ץ אַתָּ֔ה אֶתְּנָה־לְ⁠ךָ֥ כֶ֖רֶם תַּחְתָּ֑י⁠ו וַ⁠יֹּ֕אמֶר לֹֽא־אֶתֵּ֥ן לְ⁠ךָ֖ אֶת־כַּרְמִֽ⁠י
6.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [and I asked him to give me his vineyard for silver and told him that if he preferred, I would give a vineyard to him in its place. But he said that he would not give his vineyard to me]

7.note: Jezebel is repeating the pronoun **you** in order to stress Ahab’s personal role as king **over Israel**. See how you translated the similar expression “you, you swore” in 1:17. Alternate translation: [you are the one who is king over Israel]
Here, the **heart** represents a person’s feelings. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and feel happy]

Jezebel is repeating the pronoun **I** in order to stress the personal role that she will take in getting **the vineyard of Naboth** for Ahab. Alternate translation: [I will personally get the vineyard of Naboth for you]

8.note: The statement that Jezebel wrote these letters **in the name of Ahab** indicates that she signed his name to them, but it also means more than that. Ahab’s **name** also represents his person, so the statement means that Jezebel wrote these letters as if Ahab had written them himself. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [pretending that Ahab himself had written them]

The author is using these phrases to specify that Jezebel sent these letters specifically to the **elders** and **nobles** who lived in the same city as Naboth did, not to Israelite elders and nobles generally. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [who lived in the same city as Naboth did]

9.note: Proclaiming a **fast** was a symbolic action by which the leaders of a community called its members to attend to something that was very important, even more important than eating on that day. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explain the significance of this action in the text of your translation or in a footnote. Alternate translation: [Proclaim that on a certain day the people of your city should not eat, because they have a very important matter to address]

Jezebel was using the term **head** to mean the front of the crowd of **people** whom the elders and nobles would gather. If this term does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly, here and in verse 12. Alternate translation: [and seat Naboth in front of the crowd of people you gather]

Jezebel could mean: (1) that she wants the elders and nobles to put Naboth in the position of a criminal defendant. Alternate translation: [and seat Naboth in front of the crowd as an accused person] or (2) that she wants the elders and nobles to put Naboth in a seat of honor to suggest that, if not for the accusations that would then be brought against him, they would consider him a leading member of the community. In other words, this was to be a false show of impartiality. Alternate translation: [and seat Naboth in a place of honor to show that you have nothing against him personally]

10.note: To translate this expression here and in verse 13, see how you translated the similar expression in 1:52. Alternate translation: [very wicked men]
If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [saying that he blessed God and the king]

It is likely that the original reading here was “cursed” and that scribes changed it to **blessed** in order to avoid the uncomfortable language of a person cursing God. (It would not have been a capital crime if Naboth had blessed God and the king, but it would have been a capital crime if he had cursed them.) Many versions of the Bible read “cursed” here, since this is the kind of change that scribes are known to have made in similar cases. If a translation of the Bible exists in your region, you may wish to use the reading that it uses, here and in verse 13. If a translation of the Bible does not exist in your region, you may wish to use the reading of the ULT. Alternate translation: [You cursed God and the king]

11.note: The expression **was written** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [just as she had written]

13.note: This expression may seem to contain extra information that would not be natural to express in your language. If so, you could shorten it. Alternate translation: [and they stoned him]

14.note: The expression **has been stoned** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [We have stoned Naboth]

15.note: The expression **had been stoned** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the Jezreelites had stoned Naboth, and he had died]
To translate this expression and the similar ones in verses 16 and 18, see how you translated the similar expression in 1:13. Alternate translation: [Take action]

15.q: רֵ֞שׁ אֶת־כֶּ֣רֶם ׀ נָב֣וֹת הַ⁠יִּזְרְעֵאלִ֗י אֲשֶׁ֤ר מֵאֵן֙ לָ⁠תֶת־לְ⁠ךָ֣ בְ⁠כֶ֔סֶף כִּ֣י אֵ֥ין נָב֛וֹת חַ֖י כִּי־מֵֽת
15.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you could reverse the order of these phrases, since the second phrase gives the reason for the result that the first phrase describes. Alternate translation: [Since Naboth is not alive, but he is dead, possess the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite that he refused to give to you for silver]

These two phrases mean basically the same thing. The second emphasizes the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could combine them and express the emphasis in another way. Alternate translation: [Naboth is certainly dead]

17.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 6:11. Alternate translation: [Then Yahweh spoke a message to Elijah]

18.note: By **the king of Israel, who is in Samaria**, Yahweh means Ahab, who was the king of Israel and whose capital city was Samaria. He does not mean that Ahab is in Samaria at the time he is speaking to Elijah, since Ahab is in Jezreel at this time. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [the king who rules Israel from Samaria]
See how you translated the similar expression in 1:14. Alternate translation: [Listen]
See how you translated the similar expression in 1:25. Alternate translation: [where he has gone]

19.q: וְ⁠דִבַּרְתָּ֨ אֵלָ֜י⁠ו לֵ⁠אמֹ֗ר כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הֲ⁠רָצַ֖חְתָּ וְ⁠גַם־יָרָ֑שְׁתָּ וְ⁠דִבַּרְתָּ֨ אֵלָ֜י⁠ו לֵ⁠אמֹ֗ר כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה בִּ⁠מְק֗וֹם אֲשֶׁ֨ר לָקְק֤וּ הַ⁠כְּלָבִים֙ אֶת־דַּ֣ם נָב֔וֹת יָלֹ֧קּוּ הַ⁠כְּלָבִ֛ים אֶת־דָּמְ⁠ךָ֖ גַּם־אָֽתָּה
19.note: There are three levels of quotation in each sentence here. The author is quoting what Yahweh said to Elijah (level 1), continuing from the previous verse. Yahweh tells Elijah what he wants him to say to Ahab (level 2). This includes direct quotations from Yahweh himself (level 3). Use the appropriate punctuation in your language to mark these levels of quotation. Alternatively, you could translate this so that there are not second-level or third-level quotations (see the Quotes within Quotes note).

19.q: וְ⁠דִבַּרְתָּ֨ אֵלָ֜י⁠ו לֵ⁠אמֹ֗ר כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הֲ⁠רָצַ֖חְתָּ וְ⁠גַם־יָרָ֑שְׁתָּ וְ⁠דִבַּרְתָּ֨ אֵלָ֜י⁠ו לֵ⁠אמֹ֗ר כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה בִּ⁠מְק֗וֹם אֲשֶׁ֨ר לָקְק֤וּ הַ⁠כְּלָבִים֙ אֶת־דַּ֣ם נָב֔וֹת יָלֹ֧קּוּ הַ⁠כְּלָבִ֛ים אֶת־דָּמְ⁠ךָ֖ גַּם־אָֽתָּה
19.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [And you shall tell him that I say that he has murdered and also taken possession. And you shall tell him that I say that in the place where the dogs licked the blood of Naboth, the dogs will lick his blood, even his]

Yahweh is using the question form to express strong condemnation and accusation rather than to ask for information. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [You have murdered and also taken possession!]

Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [You have murdered a man and also taken possession of his property!]

By **even you**, Yahweh is stressing to Ahab that the punishment he describes will indeed happen to him. One possible implication is that even though Ahab is a king, he will not escape this judgment. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [even though you are a king]

20.note: Ahab is using the question form for emphasis. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [So, you have found me, my enemy!]

Ahab is using **Have you found me** as a common expression of his culture to mean “So, you have caught me” or “You have discovered what I have done.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Have you apprehended me] or [Have you discovered what I did]

Ahab is calling Elijah **my enemy** to mean that Elijah has come as the avenger of Ahab’s crime against Naboth. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [my avenger]

Elijah is using **you have sold yourself** as a common expression of his culture to mean that Ahab has allowed doing evil to take complete control of his life. If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [you have surrendered yourself completely to doing evil] or [you have given in completely to doing evil]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **evil**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [what is evil]
See how you translated the similar expression in 3:10. Alternate translation: [in the judgment of Yahweh]

21.note: This is the beginning of a direct quotation from Yahweh. In your translation, use a natural way of introducing direct quotations in your language. Alternate translation: [Thus says Yahweh, ‘Behold me]

21.q: הִנְ⁠נִ֨י מבי אֵלֶ֨י⁠ךָ֙ רָעָ֔ה וּ⁠בִעַרְתִּ֖י אַחֲרֶ֑י⁠ךָ וְ⁠הִכְרַתִּ֤י לְ⁠אַחְאָב֙ מַשְׁתִּ֣ין בְּ⁠קִ֔יר וְ⁠עָצ֥וּר וְ⁠עָז֖וּב בְּ⁠יִשְׂרָאֵֽל
21.note: See how you translated all of the similar expressions in 14:10. Alternate translation: [I am about to bring harm on you, and I will destroy you completely, yes, I will cause someone to kill every single one of the men in your family]

21.q: הִנְ⁠נִ֨י מבי אֵלֶ֨י⁠ךָ֙ רָעָ֔ה וּ⁠בִעַרְתִּ֖י אַחֲרֶ֑י⁠ךָ וְ⁠הִכְרַתִּ֤י לְ⁠אַחְאָב֙ מַשְׁתִּ֣ין בְּ⁠קִ֔יר וְ⁠עָצ֥וּר וְ⁠עָז֖וּב בְּ⁠יִשְׂרָאֵֽל
21.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [Yahweh says that he is about to bring harm on you, and he will destroy you completely, yes, he will cause someone to kill every single one of the men in your family]

Yahweh is speaking of **Ahab** in the third person, even though he is addressing him directly through Elijah. Yahweh is doing that because he is making a solemn declaration. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in the second person. Alternate translation: [from you]

22.q: וְ⁠נָתַתִּ֣י אֶת־בֵּיתְ⁠ךָ֗ כְּ⁠בֵית֙ יָרָבְעָ֣ם בֶּן־נְבָ֔ט וּ⁠כְ⁠בֵ֖ית בַּעְשָׁ֣א בֶן־אֲחִיָּ֑ה אֶל־הַ⁠כַּ֨עַס֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הִכְעַ֔סְתָּ וַֽ⁠תַּחֲטִ֖א אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל
22.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [He says that he will make your house like the house of Jeroboam, the son of Nebat, and like the house of Baasha, the son of Ahijah, because of the provocation by which you have provoked him, and you have caused Israel to sin]

Yahweh is speaking as if the families of Ahab, Jeroboam, and Baasha were each actually a **house**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [your family like the family of Jeroboam … and like the family of Baasha]
See how you translated the similar expression in 15:30. Alternate translation: [because you have provoked me so severely]

23.q: לֵ⁠אמֹ֑ר הַ⁠כְּלָבִ֛ים יֹאכְל֥וּ אֶת־אִיזֶ֖בֶל בְּ⁠חֵ֥ל יִזְרְעֶֽאל
23.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [saying that dogs will eat Jezebel at the rampart of Jezreel]

24.note: Yahweh is once again speaking of **Ahab** in the third person, even though he is addressing him directly, because he is making a solemn declaration. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in the second person. Alternate translation: [the who belongs to you who dies]
See how you translated this expression in 14:11 and 16:4. Alternate translation: [out in the open]

25.q: אֲשֶׁ֣ר הִתְמַכֵּ֔ר לַ⁠עֲשׂ֥וֹת הָ⁠רַ֖ע בְּ⁠עֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה
25.note: See how you translated all of the similar expression in 21:20. Alternate translation: [who surrendered himself completely to do what was evil in the judgment of Yahweh]

26.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 2:3. Alternate translation: [by living the way idol-worshipers live]

In this verse, the word **Amorite** is singular in form, but it refers to all of the Amorites as a group. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use the plural form of “Amorite.” Alternate translation: [the Amorites]
See how you translated the similar expression in 14:24. Alternate translation: [for the sake of]
See how you translated the similar expression in [6:1](ta:06). Alternate translation: [the Israelites]

27.note: Here, the expression **these words** represents what Elijah said by using words. If it would be clearer in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [what Elijah said]

Ahab’s actions of tearing his garments, wearing sackcloth day and night, fasting, and walking softly were symbolic actions by which he showed his repentance and mourning for his sins. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explain the significance of these actions in the text of your translation or in a footnote. Alternate translation: [that to show his sorrow for his sins, he tore his garments, put sackcloth upon his flesh, fasted, lay down in sackcloth, and walked humbly]

28.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 6:11. Alternate translation: [And Yahweh spoke a message to Elijah]

29.note: Here Yahweh is using the question form to draw Elijah’s attention to what has happened. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [You must have seen that Ahab has humbled himself from to my face.]

Yahweh is using **from my face** as a common expression of the culture to mean “in my presence.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [in my presence … in my presence]

In each instance here, **days** represents a period of time, specifically the lifetime of a person. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [during his lifetime. During the lifetime of his son]
Here, **house** represents the family of Ahab. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [his family]
